economy.summary: His campaign platform says he fights for good-paying jobs, thriving small businesses, and an economy where hard work pays off for everyone. It also says he fights for affordable housing and home repair assistance so families are not pushed out of their communities by rising costs.
economy.short: Fights for good-paying jobs, small businesses, affordable housing.

taxes.summary: Touted education funding increases in the 2024-25 state budget as a win for Reading and other central Pennsylvania cities, and supported creating a City Revitalization and Improvement Zone in Reading, a program in which state and local taxes collected within the zone repay debt on economic development projects.
taxes.short: Touts 2024-25 education funding; backed Reading tax-financed redevelopment zone.

abortion.summary: Voted against Senate Bill 106 in July 2022, a package of proposed constitutional amendments that included a provision stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant a right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion.
abortion.short: Voted against amendment declaring no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: His campaign platform says he fights for full, fair funding for public schools so every student can reach their full potential, and cites $29 million secured for Reading schools in the 2025-26 budget.
education.short: Fights for full, fair public school funding.

healthcare.summary: His campaign platform says healthcare is a right, not a privilege, and that he is fighting to expand access to affordable healthcare and mental health services for every family in the district.
healthcare.short: Fighting to expand affordable healthcare and mental health services.

energy.summary: His campaign platform says he is fighting for environmental justice so that every neighborhood has clean air, clean water, and a healthy environment; the platform does not address energy production.
energy.short: Fighting for clean air, clean water, environmental justice.

guns.summary: Voted in May 2023 for House Bill 714, which would require background checks for private sales of long guns in Pennsylvania by repealing an exemption in state law; the bill passed the House 109-92.
guns.short: Voted for background checks on private long-gun sales.
